Create a Frequentist or Bayesian Quantitative Decision Rule

Source: R/f_design_qtd.R
getDesignQuantitative.Rd

Constructs a fixed-design quantitative decision rule. Its class selects the calculation in the common operating-characteristics functions.

Usage

getDesignQuantitative(
  targetValue,
  lowerReferenceValue = 0,
  upperPercentile = 0.9,
  lowerPercentile = 0.2,
  bayesian = FALSE,
  useSignificanceAndTarget = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  go = NULL,
  stop = NULL,
  indeterminate1 = NULL,
  percentileMapping = "quantile"
)

Arguments

targetValue

Single target effect on the beneficial-effect scale.

lowerReferenceValue

Single lower reference effect; default zero.

upperPercentile

Upper percentile in (0, 1); default 0.9.

lowerPercentile

Lower percentile in (0, upperPercentile); default 0.2.

bayesian

Whether to construct a Bayesian rule. Explicit criteria imply TRUE when this argument is omitted.

useSignificanceAndTarget

Construct a dual significance/target rule.

alpha

Two-sided frequentist significance level or Bayesian posterior tail probability in (0, 0.5); default 0.05. These are different conventions.

go, stop, indeterminate1

Criteria from getQuantitativeDecisionThresholds(). Supply all three without reference values, percentiles or shortcut options.

percentileMapping

Bayesian interpretation: "quantile" (default) or "posteriorProbability". Stored in the design for reproducibility.

Value

A TrialDesignPlanQuantitative or TrialDesignPlanQuantitativeBayes, inheriting from TrialDesignPlanQuantitativeBase and ParameterSet.

Details

For mapping "quantile", Go requires P(effect > LRV) > 1-lowerPercentile and P(effect > TV) > 1-upperPercentile. Stop requires P(effect <= LRV) > lowerPercentile and P(effect <= TV) > upperPercentile. This follows by comparing posterior quantiles with the references, and agrees with normal CI decisions in the diffuse-prior limit. It differs from the exploratory prototype mapping.

Mapping "posteriorProbability" is a different rule: the beneficial-tail Go thresholds are upperPercentile at LRV and lowerPercentile at TV, and Stop uses their complements. For both mappings, Indeterminate 1 fails the LRV criterion and passes TV. Indeterminate 2 is the complement of Go, Stop and Indeterminate 1, including exact probability-threshold ties. Comparisons are strict, following RBesT; ties can have positive sampling probability for rates.

The significance/target shortcut uses lowerPercentile = alpha/2 and upperPercentile = 0.5 for frequentist rules. Bayesian rules require posterior probabilities 1-alpha at LRV and 0.5 at TV, independently of percentileMapping. The shortcut stores the canonical quantile mapping for reproducibility. The two shortcuts are not claimed to be equivalent: for example 95 percent two-sided confidence corresponds to a 97.5 percent one-sided tail probability.

All explicit categories must be provably pairwise incompatible by monotonicity of a continuous posterior CDF. Potential overlaps are rejected; a particular prior might permit additional disjoint rules that this conservative validation cannot certify. No category precedence is introduced. When defining custom intermediate criteria, explicitly exclude futility, as in the RBesT examples. Reference effects always use the beneficial direction, also for decreasing rates.

See also

getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans(), getOperatingCharacteristicsRates(), https://opensource.nibr.com/RBesT/reference/decision2S.html

Examples

rule <- getDesignQuantitative(targetValue = 1)
bayes <- getDesignQuantitative(targetValue = 1, bayesian = TRUE)
dual <- getDesignQuantitative(targetValue = 1, bayesian = TRUE,
    useSignificanceAndTarget = TRUE)
